source.title: Using the Frattini Subgroup and Independent Generating Sets to Study RWPRI Geometries
source.version: Complete nine-page published primary PDF; two prior mirror responses identical
source.reading: Complete extraction pages1-9 (printed169-177), all statements/proofs/discussions/references read during this extension
read_limits: No newly regenerated PDF extraction or independent visual formula-layout reconstruction.
Gaschütz1953, Archer2004 and Eick algorithm originals were not acquired or independently rechecked.

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: For B<=G and Phi=Phi(G), a family (s_i) is an independent generating family of G relative to B iff (Phi s_i) is an independent generating family of G/Phi relative to BPhi/Phi.
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Elementary finite group theory; Zorn for relative finite-generation infinite extension

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: A firm RWPRI coset geometry satisfies Phi(G)<=H_i for every type i, including infinite G.
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Zorn for infinite groups; elementary subgroup theory

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: If N is normal in G and N<=H_i for every type of a coset pregeometry, that pregeometry is isomorphic to the coset pregeometry (G/N,(H_i/N)).
A firm RWPRI coset geometry (G,(H_i)) is isomorphic to (G/Phi(G),(H_i/Phi(G))).
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Zorn for infinite groups; subgroup correspondence

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: Every firm RWPRI geometry is isomorphic to a firm RWPRI geometry for a Frattini-free group.
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Zorn for infinite groups; subgroup correspondence

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: A rank-two coset pregeometry (G,(H_1,H_2)) is a direct sum iff H_1 H_2=G.
For proper U,W<F_p^k with W not contained in U, if U is maximal and U intersect W is maximal in U, then W is maximal in F_p^k.
A firm coset geometry of a finite p-group is RWPRI iff it is RPRI.
all_numbered_items.proof: E0,E2,E3,E5 and existing Compress_A Theorem R(b)
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Finite-p-group Frattini quotient is elementary abelian; elementary vector spaces

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: A firm RWPRI coset geometry of a p-group is a direct sum of primitive rank-one geometries. The source section fixes finite p-groups, although this theorem sentence omits the word finite.
all_numbered_items.proof: E0,E2,E3,E5 and existing Compress_A Theorem R(b)
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Finite-p-group Frattini quotient is elementary abelian; elementary vector spaces

all_numbered_items.full_normalized_formulation: A finite Frattini-free F with socle S=A times D (abelian and nonabelian simple factors respectively) has F=A semidirect K, K<=Aut(S)=Aut(A) times Aut(D), D=Inn(S)<=K, and K acts semisimply on A; the intersection of maximal K-invariant subgroups of A is trivial.
all_numbered_items.retained_background: Gaschütz, Math.Z.58(1953),160-170; original not independently read in this extension

unnumbered_target_items.full_normalized_formulation: For every residue at a flag of type J, Phi(H_J)<=H_J intersect H_i for every remaining type i; this is necessary, not sufficient.

The largest normal subgroup of G contained in B is core_G(B)=intersection_i core_G(H_i); quotienting yields the faithful coset action, and for firm RWPRI geometries this kernel contains Phi(G). The separately cited Archer2004 classification at the end of this section is retained, not newly proved.

reused_core.interface: H_J=<B,s_i:i not in J>; strong relative independence
reused_core.new_application: Frattini containment makes P/B elementary abelian; the existing generating equality then gives a coordinate basis and every p-group parabolic.

necessary_new_proof: E0: finite-rank RWPRI implies flag transitivity
E1/E2: relative maximal-overgroup existence and normal-subgroup ladder
E4: Frattini transport of relative generators with valid infinite hypothesis and counterexample to unrestricted converse
E5: short coordinate specialization using R(b), not an imported p-group geometry classification

Zorn lemma for the explicitly infinite claims

correction.counterexample: G=C_(p^infinity) times C2, Phi(G)=C_(p^infinity) times1, B=1; the second-factor generator generates G/Phi(G) but not G.
